column2: 英语 twise ← 中古英语 twies ← 古英语 twīġes（两次），由 twīwa（两次）＋ 副词属格词尾 -es 构成
column3: on two occasions, or two times as much
column5: I have read it twice already.|This box weighs twice as much.
column6: counted through two times rather than once – 数过两遍，不是一遍
column7: 两回：发生或做了两次|两倍：数量上是原来的二倍

column2: 中古英语 twinne ← 古英语 ġetwinn（孪生的）← 原始日耳曼语 *twinaz（成双的）← 原始印欧语 *dwóh₁（二）
column3: one of two children born at the same birth, or forming a matching pair
column5: Her twin lives in Australia.|The hotel has twin beds.
column6: one of two that came into being together and match – 同时产生、彼此相配的那两个中的一个
column7: 孪生之一：同胎所生的两人中的一个|成对的：两件相同、配成一套的

column2: 中古英语 twinclen ← 古英语 twinclian（闪动），即 twink（眨、闪）＋ 反复体后缀 -le；与德语 zwinkern（眨眼）同族
column3: to shine with a light that keeps changing
column5: Stars twinkled above the ridge.|Her eyes twinkled at the joke.
column6: a light that keeps going bright and dim by turns – 光一亮一暗地轮着来
column7: 闪耀：光时强时弱地发出|明灭：亮与暗交替这个过程|眼中放光：把这种光用到人的眼神上

column2: 中古英语 twist ← 古英语 *twist（见于复合词）← 原始日耳曼语 *twistaz，由 *twi-（二、双）派生；与 twine、between 同支
column3: to turn something around itself, or an unexpected change
column5: She twisted the cloth to wring it out.|The story took an odd twist.
column6: turning something around its own length – 让一件东西绕着自身转
column7: 拧：两端反向转动|扭转：把方向或局面转过来|转折：事情走向忽然拐了一下

column2: 中古英语 two ← 古英语 twā（twēġen 的阴性与中性形）← 原始日耳曼语 *twai ← 原始印欧语 *dwóh₁（二）
column3: the number that comes after one
column5: Two cups stood side by side.|He waited two hours for the bus.
column6: the count reached by adding one to one – 一再加一得出的那个数
column7: 二：作为数字本身|两：与量词连用时的说法

column2: 由 type（打字）＋ writer（书写器）复合而成；type 一支 ← 拉丁语 typus ← 希腊语 typos（打出的印记）
column3: a machine with keys that prints letters onto paper
column5: She learned to use a typewriter at school.|An old typewriter sat on the desk.
column6: a machine that stamps each letter onto paper as a key is struck – 按一个键就把一个字母压到纸上的机器

column2: 1588 年始见英语（作 Touffon），经葡萄牙语 tufão 传入 ← 阿拉伯语 tufan（大风暴）；拼写受希腊语 typhon（旋风）影响
column3: a violent tropical storm in the western Pacific
column5: The typhoon shut the port for days.|Typhoon season begins in July.
column6: a huge spinning storm that forms over warm western Pacific seas – 西太平洋暖海面上生成的巨大旋转风暴

column2: 中古英语 ugly，借自古诺尔斯语 uggligr（可怕的、样子骇人的）← uggr（惧、忧）；14 世纪末词义由「可怕」转为「难看」
column3: unpleasant to look at
column5: The building is genuinely ugly.|The argument turned ugly within minutes.
column6: unpleasant enough to look at that one turns away – 看着不舒服，让人想避开
column7: 丑的：形貌不好看|难看的：同义，语气缓些|难堪的：把这种不适用到场面上，指局面变糟

column2: 源自中世纪拉丁语 ultimatus（最末的），是 ultimō（终结）的完成被动分词 ← ultimus（最后的）
column3: final, or most fundamental
column5: That was his ultimate offer.|Safety is the ultimate concern.
column6: the last one, beyond which there is no further – 最后这一个，再往后没有了
column7: 最终的：排在最末、不再有下一个|根本的：追到底层、再往下无可追的

column2: 由 ultra-（超出）＋ violet（紫）构成；violet 一支 ← 古法语 violete ← 拉丁语 viola（紫罗兰）
column3: of the invisible light just beyond the violet end of the spectrum
column5: Ultraviolet light damages the skin.|The note glowed under ultraviolet lamps.
column6: light lying just past violet, where the eye can no longer follow – 排在紫之外、眼睛已跟不上的那段光

column2: 借自意大利语 ombrella（遮阳伞）← 晚期拉丁语 umbrella（受 umbra「阴影」影响）← 拉丁语 umbella，是 umbra 的指小形
column3: a folding frame covered in cloth, held up against rain
column5: Take an umbrella; it looks like rain.|The scheme acts as an umbrella for smaller charities.
column6: a small canopy raised overhead to keep rain off – 撑在头上遮雨的那片小顶棚
column7: 雨伞：撑开遮雨的那件器物|保护伞：把这层遮护用到组织或势力上

column2: 中古英语 uncle ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 uncle／古法语 oncle ← 拉丁语 avunculus（舅父，字面「小外祖父」）；取代了古英语 ēam 与 fædera
column3: the brother of one's father or mother
column5: My uncle taught me to fish.|She stayed with her uncle that summer.
column6: a parent's brother, one generation up and to the side – 父母的兄弟，长一辈而不在直系上
column7: 叔伯：父亲的兄弟|舅舅：母亲的兄弟

column2: 中古英语 under ← 古英语 under ← 原始日耳曼语 *under ← 原始印欧语 *(H)n̥dʰér（在下）与 *h₁entér（在内）合流
column3: in or to a position below something
column5: The cat slept under the table.|Children under six pay nothing.
column6: at a level below the thing named – 位置或程度低于所说的那个
column7: 在…下面：空间上处于其下|低于：数量或年龄不到那个数|在…之中：处在某种状态或管辖之下

column2: 由 under-（不足）＋ estimate（估计）构成；estimate 一支 ← 拉丁语 aestimare（估价）
column3: to think something is smaller or weaker than it really is
column5: Do not underestimate the cost of repairs.|They underestimated their opponents badly.
column6: setting the figure lower than the thing actually is – 把数量或分量估得比实际低
column7: 低估：估得不足|看轻：把对方的能力或分量想少了

column2: 中古英语 undergon ← 古英语 undergān（经历、受），即 under-（在下）＋ go（走）
column3: to experience something, especially something unpleasant
column5: She underwent surgery last week.|The building underwent major repairs.
column6: passing through something done to you – 从某件加在自己身上的事里过一遍
column7: 经历：从头到尾经过某个过程|受到：被动地承受某种处置

column2: 中古英语 undergrounde，即 under ＋ ground；ground 一支 ← 古英语 grund（地面、底）← 原始日耳曼语 *grunduz
column3: below the surface of the earth, or kept secret
column5: An underground stream feeds the well.|They ran an underground newspaper.
column6: lying below the surface, out of sight – 处在地面以下，看不见
column7: 地下的：位置在地表之下|秘密的：像埋在地下一样不让人知道

column2: 中古英语 underlien ← 古英语 underliċġan（在下、隶属），即 under ＋ lie
column3: to lie beneath, or to form the basis of something
column5: Older rock underlies the whole valley.|Distrust underlies the whole dispute.
column6: lying below and holding up what shows on top – 躺在下面，托住露在上面的那一层
column7: 位于…之下：实际处在其下方|构成…的基础：看不见却支着上面那件事

column2: 由 under-（在下）＋ line（线）构成；line 一支 ← 古英语 līne ← 拉丁语 linea（线）
column3: to draw a line under words, or to make a point stand out
column5: Underline the key terms in red.|The report underlines the need for care.
column6: drawing a line beneath so the eye stops there – 在底下划一道，让眼睛在那儿停住
column7: 划线：在字下面画一条线|强调：把某一点特意点出来，如同划线

column2: 由 underlie ＋ -ing 构成；underlie 一支 ← 古英语 underliċġan（在下、隶属）
column3: present beneath the surface, though not obvious
column5: The underlying cause was never found.|Beneath the calm lay underlying tension.
column6: there beneath, holding things up without showing – 在底下托着，却不露出来
column7: 潜在的：存在却未显现|根本的：处在最底层、决定上面那些的

column2: 由 under-（在下）＋ mine（挖坑道）构成；mine 一支 ← 古法语 miner（挖）
column3: to weaken something gradually from below
column5: Gossip undermined her authority in the office.|Water had undermined the wall for years.
column6: digging away what holds something up, out of sight – 在看不见处把支撑挖走
column7: 暗中削弱：不动声色地使之变弱|掏空根基：把底下的支撑掏走，表面还看不出

column2: 中古英语 undernethe ← 古英语 underneoþan（在下面）← 原始日耳曼语 *underniþer，即 under-＋ neath（下）
column3: below or beneath something, especially hidden there
column5: The key was underneath the mat.|She wore a jumper underneath.
column6: tucked below something and covered by it – 压在某物之下、被它盖着
column7: 在下面：位置处于其下|底下：口语说法，多指被遮住的那一侧

column2: 中古英语 understanden ← 古英语 understandan ← 原始日耳曼语 *understandaną（站在其间、领会），即 under-（在其间）＋ stand（站）
column3: to know what something means or how it works
column5: I do not understand the question.|He understands how the engine works.
column6: seeing how the parts stand together, so the whole makes sense – 看清各部分怎样搭在一起，整件事就通了
column7: 懂：知道其意思|理解：想清了其中道理|领会：把话外之意也接住

column2: 中古英语 understandinge ← 古英语 understanding（智力、领会），即 understand ＋ -ing
column3: the ability to know what something means, or an informal agreement
column5: She has a good understanding of the law.|They reached an understanding after talks.
column6: grasping how things fit, and the agreement that grasp allows – 弄清事情如何相合，以及由此达成的一致
column7: 理解力：能弄懂事理的那份能力|共识：双方对同一件事看法一致|谅解：明白对方处境后不再计较

column2: 中古英语 undertaken，即 under-（在下）＋ take（拿），仿早期 undernim 而造
column3: to agree to do something and take responsibility for it
column5: They undertook to finish by June.|She undertook the repairs herself.
column6: taking a task onto yourself and standing behind it – 把一件事接到自己身上，并为它负责
column7: 着手：开始动手做|答应：应下这件事|担起：把责任接过来自己扛

column2: 中古英语 undōn ← 古英语 ondōn ← 原始西日耳曼语 *andadōn，即 un-（反向）＋ do（做）
column3: to open what was fastened, or to reverse what was done
column5: He undid the top button.|You cannot undo what was said.
column6: working an action backwards so it no longer holds – 把做过的动作倒着走一遍，使它不再成立
column7: 解开：把系紧的松开|撤销：把已做的取消，使回到原状

column2: 中古英语 unesy，即 un-（不）＋ easy（安适的）；并与中古英语 unethe（不易的）合流
column3: anxious and not able to relax
column5: He felt uneasy about the plan.|An uneasy silence filled the room.
column6: unable to settle because something feels wrong – 心里觉着不对，安不下来
column7: 不安的：心里悬着，放不下|局促的：身处其中觉着别扭、不自在

column2: 由 un-（不）＋ expected（预料到的）构成；expect 一支 ← 拉丁语 exspectare（张望、等待）
column3: not thought likely to happen
column5: His visit was completely unexpected.|An unexpected bill arrived on Friday.
column6: turning up without having been counted on – 事先没算上，却出现了
column7: 意外的：出乎预想之外|没料到的：事先完全没想到会这样

column2: 中古英语 unfolden ← 古英语 unfealdan（展开），即 un-（反向）＋ fold（折）
column3: to open something folded, or to become gradually clear
column5: She unfolded the map on the bonnet.|The story unfolded over three days.
column6: opening the folds so what was inside comes into view – 把折起的层次打开，里面的就露出来
column7: 展开：把折着的打开|铺开：展开后摊平在面上|逐渐显露：事情一层层显出来，如同展开

column2: 中古英语 unlic ← 古英语 unġelīċ（不相似的）← 原始日耳曼语 *ungalīkaz，即 un-（不）＋ like（相似）
column3: different from, or not typical of
column5: Unlike her sister, she enjoys crowds.|That remark was quite unlike him.
column6: set against something and found not to match – 与某物相比，对不上
column7: 与…不同：两者相较有别|不像：与某人平素的样子不符

column2: 中古英语 unlykely，即 un-（不）＋ likely（可能的）；likely 一支 ← 古诺尔斯语 líkligr（像样的、可能的）
column3: probably not going to happen or be true
column5: Rain is unlikely before evening.|It seems an unlikely explanation.
column6: having little to suggest it will come about – 没有多少迹象显示它会发生
column7: 不太可能的：发生的机会很小|未必的：不一定如此，留有反面余地
